target: APG modal dialog semantics, accessible naming and aria-modal truthfulness
observed_behavior: The APG modal-dialog pattern documents a dialog container with role dialog, aria-modal=true, all controls required to operate the dialog inside that container, and an accessible name using aria-labelledby referring to a visible title or aria-label. It describes aria-describedby as optional and suited to simple description text; it advises omitting it for substantial semantically structured dialog content. The pattern cautions to mark a dialog modal only when application behavior prevents outside interaction for all users and visual styling obscures the content outside it, since an incorrect aria-modal claim can hide outside content from some assistive-technology users.
context: W07 B3 K3 read-only APG WAI-ARIA Roles, States, and Properties; About This Pattern; first-party non-normative explanatory guidance, bounded to qualified APG pattern and exceptions.
limitations: This is APG explanatory implementation guidance, not a normative WCAG success criterion, WHATWG platform rule, or proof of browser/AT support.
aria-modal=true alone is not evidence of functional modality; both effective outside-interaction prevention and visual obscuring are stated prerequisites in this guidance.
aria-describedby is optional, not a universal mandate; complex semantic content is a documented non-applicability case.
The unavailable standalone APG /patterns/dialog/ page must not be used to invent independent non-modal guidance.
Only the public APG page was inspected; no application source or runtime was tested.
